subject: Re: ACME - next steps: observability & hyperscaler comparison
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@acmepay.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jan 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed tests (observability + hyperscaler comparison)

Thanks again for the time today, Sofia — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get you the comparative data you asked for: 

Summary notes from discovery:
- Primary goal: validate inference economics and operational visibility for Acme Payments' fraud scoring pipeline (low-latency, high-throughput).
- Key comparators: hyperscaler inference APIs (AWS Bedrock / Azure OpenAI) + current Anthropic endpoint.
- Must evaluate: latency p50/p95 under realistic batch sizes, end-to-end tracing (request -> model -> downstream), cost per inference, and how observability surfaces model failures/quality regressions.
- Constraints: procurement + legal will need SOC2 + evidence of KMS integration and log retention policies.

Proposed next tests (high-level):
1) Synthetic load run: 1k req/s sustained for 1 hour at your typical payload size. Measure p50/p95, tail latency, error rates.
2) Trace-level run: instrument end-to-end tracing (we provide tracing headers) to verify span depth and latency attribution.
3) Cost benchmark: identical prompt set across providers to measure token and per-request cost.
4) KV/prefix-cache scenario: validate cold vs warm latencies for repeated user contexts.

What we can provide immediately:
- Temporary test credentials and a pre-built Grafana dashboard showing token usage, latency buckets, and sampling traces.
- A short test matrix (attached) and a one-page mutual action plan (attached: 20260128-acme-mop.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm which of the above tests you want us to prioritize (synthetic load vs trace depth).
- We spin up test creds and run a 1-hour synthetic load (we recommend starting with synthetic load + trace run).
- We loop in Dev (cc'd) to help with instrumentation and providing the Redwood tracing headers.

Attachments: 20260128-acme-mop.pdf (MOP overview)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c

Thanks — I’ll wait for your preference on the test order and any procurement constraints we should be aware of.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@acmepay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Brad Thompson <brad.t@acmepay.com>, Acme Payments Procurement <procurement@acmepay.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jan 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed tests (observability + hyperscaler comparison)

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. We're very interested in the synthetic load and trace-level runs. A couple of clarifying items from our side before we schedule: 

- Procurement: Brad and our procurement team will need a ballpark for trial overage protection and any terms for the trial creds.
- Security: we need to validate KMS support and whether logs can be routed to our SIEM (we can share requirements). SOC2 docs would be great.
- Timeline: our eng team can run tests next week (Feb 2–4). Would you be able to have creds and a short-runbook by then?

Please include any instrumentation examples — our infra lead (Brad) will want that. If we're good on security signals (KMS + SOC2 evidence) and cost directionally looks better than hyperscalers, we'll move to a procurement PO shortly after.

Cheers,
Sofia
Senior Product Manager — Risk
Acme Payments
sofia.alvarez@acmepay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@acmepay.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed tests (observability + hyperscaler comparison)

Appreciate the quick reply, Sofia — we can absolutely have creds and a runbook ready for Feb 2.

Attached is a test matrix (acme-optooling-test-matrix.xlsx) that maps each test to measurable outputs and acceptance criteria. High level:
- Synthetic load: verify p50 < 60ms, p95 < 180ms under 1k req/s with batching tuned.
- Trace run: trace depth must show model inference spans + downstream DB calls; we recommend 1% trace sampling for full spans.
- Cost: side-by-side cost sheet for same prompt set across Redwood vs Bedrock vs Azure.

Security notes: we'll attach SOC2 snapshot and a short KMS integration doc. Dev will follow up with instrumentation snippets and the test credentials.

Suggested schedule:
- Feb 2: handoff + credential provisioning, quick pairing call (30m) to wire tracing headers.
- Feb 3: synthetic load + trace sampling run (engineer time: 1x Redwood engineer + 1x Acme infra).
- Feb 4: share results + cost comparison and recommended next steps.

Attachments: acme-optooling-test-matrix.xlsx

If that works, Brad/procurement — please advise on any trial terms we should include.

Best,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@acmepay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Feb 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed tests (observability + hyperscaler comparison)

Hi Sofia — quick tech notes and the instrumentation snippet we mentioned.

1) Tracing headers: send X-Redwood-Trace: <trace-id> and we'll attach full spans in sampling. We'll correlate request IDs with trace IDs and provide a mapping table in the dashboard.

2) Rate limits: for the test we'll lift production rate limits on the test creds to support 1k req/s sustained; we'll still enforce safety checks (payload size limits).

3) Sample curl (short):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST_KEY_ACME" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Trace: 7d9f3a1b-..." \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2b-opt","input":"<sample prompt>","max_tokens":128}'

4) Grafana dashboard: we'll provision a read-only dashboard with panels for token consumption, latency buckets (p50/p95/p99), error rate, and sampled traces. Dashboard link will be active with the test creds.

Attachment: redwood-test-creds.txt (contains temporary API key and dashboard link)

If you want, we can do a 20–30 minute pairing session at 9:30 PT on Feb 2 to wire up the headers and walk the dashboard layout.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
